This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of the M.V.Act 1989.
2.

The brief facts of case of the Petitioner is that:
The petitioner being minor represented by his father and natural guardian.

That on 29.01.2023 at about 4.00 to 4.05 p.m. petitioner had been a pedestrian on Haralur Village, near 7th cross road, Bengaluru city, at that time, a driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MQ-2052, Chassis No.MCANJPCY9LFA67970AL and Engine No.4077619 drove in rash and negligent manner and SCCH-5 dashed against him,
due to the said impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries on right leg and all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Lotus Multi Speciality Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and spent Rs.75,000/-
towards medical, conveyance and nourishment charges,

sentences.text: At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 10 years and student, due to the said accident, he cannot attend to his classes, resulted in loss of stress, mental shock and put to great hardship.
Out of the said accident, crime No.63/2023 is registered before the Electronic City Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC against the driver of the said car.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is owner of the car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the SCCH-5 petition and grant the compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- along with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denies the involvement of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MQ-2052 in the alleged accident.
Further denies the issuance of policy in the name of Sangeetha M. Kashyap in respect of said vehicle and submitted that, accident has taken place due to negligency of the petitioner himself.

Further submitted that, driver of the offending vehicle does not possess valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle is not having valid and effective fitness certificate as on the date of alleged accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Respondent No.2/owner has appeared and filed written statement and submitted that, claim petition SCCH-5 is bad for misjoinder and non-joinder of necessary parties, hence petition is liable to be dismissed.
Further submitted that, vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MQ-2052 is duly insured with respondent No.1 and driver of the said vehicle possessed valid and effective driving license.

Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable and further submitted that, father of the petitioner had promised that, if this respondent has paid Rs.20,000/- as the full medical expenditure, the petitioner would not claim any further amount from this respondent.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have SCCH-5 occurred on 29.01.2023 at about 4.00 to 4.05 p.m. when petitioner was a pedestrian near Haraluru Village, near 7th Cross road,
Bengaluru, at that time, one Car bearing Reg.No. KA-51-MQ-2052 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove his case, father/natural guardian of the petitioner deposed his evidence as PW-1,
examined Dr.B.Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW-2 and marked Thilak.D vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36871626/
3 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his evidence.

sentences.text: On the other hand, respondents have submitted that, there is no evidence.
Further in the cross-examination of PW-1, two SCCH-5 document have been marked i.e., Ex.D.1 and Ex.D.2 by way of confrontation.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9.
Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the above point, the father and natural guardian of the Petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1 by way of reiterating the facts narrated in the petition.
Hence, in order to avoid the repetition of facts, chief- examination of the PW-1 is not reproduced here.

In support of his case, PW-1 has SCCH-5 furnished copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch marked as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.6.
10.
Further to substantiate the petitioner case, PW-1 has examined one Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar,
sketch, charge sheet and IMV Report corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 29.01.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11. Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the SCCH-5 accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 29.01.2023 at about 4.00 to 4.05 p.m. when he had been a pedestrian on Haraluru Village,
near 7th Cross road, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the PW-1, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, PW-1 has proved the above issue SCCH-5 No.1 in favour of minor petitioner.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the PW-1, petitioner was aged about 10 years as on the date of accident.

In order to prove his age, PW-1 has produced copy of aadhar card of the petitioner marked as Ex.P.8 and copy of birth certificate of the petitioner marked as Ex.P.9, wherein date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 28.12.2013, the alleged accident is occurred on 29.01.2023.
Relying on Ex.P.8 and 9 this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 10 years as on the date of accident.
14. It is the case of the petitioner that, he has sustained fracture of right tibia, for which he was treatd conservatively.

In this regard, PW-1 has produced copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7 issued by Lotus SCCH-5 Multispeciality Center, medical prescription marked as Ex.P.10, medical bills to the tune of Rs.23,446/- marked as Ex.P.11 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.12.
15.

In support of his case, Dr.B.Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW-2 and he has exhibited OPD document marked as Ex.P.13 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.14 and he has assessed permanent physical disability of 18% of right lower limb, which is about 9% of whole body.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and not seen the MLC of the patient.
Further deposed that, in Ex.P.7 wound certificate there is no mention with regard to fracture of right tibia, but there is mention that injuries are grievous in nature.
Further deposed that, said fracture is united and he has assessed whole disability at SCCH-5 9%, which is a minimal disability.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 6% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 18% of right lower limb disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

16. Further as per the rulings reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396 in between Mallikarjun V/s. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another, wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that, "In the case of children suffering from disability on account of motor vehicle accident, the tribunals should award the compensation in the following manner;
SCCH-5 if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; upto 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; upto 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs.

entities.text: Mallikarjun V/s. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Re.1 lakh".
17. So herein this case, functional disability is assessed at 6%.
Hence, loss of future income shall be awarded at the rate of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.1,00,000/- along with other heads.

18. Further he is entitled for Rs.15,000/- for pain and sufferings, Rs.15,000/- for inconvenience caused to his parents, loss of future amenities of Rs.15,000/-, conveyance food and nourishment charges of Rs.15,000/-.
PW-1 has has produced medical bills to the tune of Rs.23,446/- marked are as Ex.P.11, petitioner is entitled for the said amount towards medical expenses.

Full and final settlement

20. Further on perusal of said admissions of PW-1 he has produced Ex.P.10 for Rs.23,466/- and he SCCH-5 also admitted Ex.D.1 and 2 documents, they are full and final settlement letter drawn on white paper.

So merely PW-1 has affixed his signature on the said two white papers, they are not sufficient to disbelieve entire case of the petitioner, because admittedly the said Ex.D.1 and Ex.D.2 are held prior to the filing of the petition and inside the court.

Ofcourse as per the admissions of PW-1, he has admitted that, as per Ex.D.1 and Ex.D.2 he has received Rs.8,500/- etc., but said admission of PW-1 have noway supports the respondent's case in any manner.

Accordingly I am of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for the reliefs as stated above i.e., for compensation and and any admissions admitted by the PW-1 in his cross-examination have not support the respondents in any manner.
SCCH-5 21

. Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of this case, this tribunal has calculated compensation as under:-
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss on account of disability 1,00,000-00 2. Pain and Sufferings 15,000-00 3. Conveyance, Nourishment and 15,000-00 Attendant Charges 4.
Medical Expenses 23,446-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,68,446/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

sentences.text:
In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.3001/213136473/00/000 which is valid for the SCCH-5 period from 31.12.2020 to 30.12.2023,
the alleged accident was occurred on 29.01.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
Though respondent No.1 has denied issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2, but they have not taken endeavours to disprove the case of the petitioner by leading evidence.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.2 shall go against respondent No.1, so that, respondent No.1/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH-5 ::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,68,446/- (Rupees One Lakh Sixty Eight Thousand Four Hundred Forty Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount, The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

On deposit of compensation amount, PW-1 i.e., father and natural guardian of the petitioner is entitled to get release Rs.50,000/- out of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.

Remaining awarded amount is ordered to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank in the name of minor Petitioner till he attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in SCCH-5 the name of minor Petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor Petitioner.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
Dictated to the stenographer directly on the computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 5th day of October, 2024)
(MANJUNATHA K.P.) VIII ADDL.
